title: Human Tasks Canvas
description: Tracks offline human tasks (interviews, observations, outreach). Created by /handoff, consumed by /log-evidence and session-start.sh. Bridges agent-executable and human-executable work.

touch_log.description: Chronological log of exchanges on this task's channel. Formalised in v0.68.0: it existed as an undocumented convention surviving only on additionalProperties, so nothing could safely read it. `direction` is what makes a task's state legible - without it an inbound and an outbound are indistinguishable, and a task where the CONTACT is waiting on YOU looks identical to one where you are waiting on them.

direction.description: Who moved. `outbound` = you contacted them. `inbound` = they contacted you. `bidirectional` = a two-way exchange captured as one entry (no reply is owed - it completed). `internal` = an observation or note with NO contact (a metric reading, a status note); these are skipped entirely when locating the last contact, so an internal note logged on top of an inbound does not conceal the owed reply. Keep the value bare - annotations belong in `purpose`, since a qualified value like 'outbound (founder-sent)' defeats the machine read this field exists for. NOT required: pre-v0.68.0 logs have none and must keep validating on upgrade; entries without it are unevaluable rather than invalid.

purpose.description: What was sent, received, or observed.

closure_reason.description: Why this was closed. Must name what happened, not how long it has been.

reopen_trigger.description: What would make this closure wrong, stated concretely enough to be checked by someone who was not there. This is the field that turns a stale closure into a detectable one.

horizon.description: When this task's outcome should be read, ISO-8601. USED IN PRACTICE AND UNDECLARED UNTIL v0.97.0 — 22 occurrences in the dogfood canvas, and canvas-health check 8c(b) reads it to decide whether an open task is genuinely stale or legitimately waiting. A field a shipped check depends on must be declared: undeclared means unvalidated, so a typo like `horizion` degrades the check silently instead of failing.

evidence_logged_to.description: Where the evidence landed. STRING OR ARRAY, and the reason is measured rather than stylistic: this was `array` only, while all seven real records in four months of dogfood use were STRINGS -- often a single anchor with a parenthetical, e.g. 'opportunities.yml#opp-005.provenance (2026-08-02 entry)'. The records were never checked because `pending_tasks` does not constrain this field at all, so the mismatch only surfaced when they were finally moved here (v0.131.0).

key_findings.description: What was learned. STRING OR ARRAY, and this one was backwards in the OPPOSITE direction from `evidence_logged_to` above: specified as a string while real records are lists of distinct findings. A schema that had both fields inverted relative to actual use is not a contract anyone was writing against.

closure_reason.description: Why this was closed. Must name what happened, not how long it has been.

reopen_trigger.description: What would make this closure wrong, stated concretely enough to be checked by someone who was not there. This is the field that turns a stale closure into a detectable one.

items.description: Tasks that closed having produced evidence. `required` was relaxed from [id, completed_at, source_class] to [id] in v0.130.0: measured against four months of real closures in the dogfood project, 47 of 61 completed tasks carried neither field, because no closure path ever populated them. A schema asserting a contract that its own producers never met is the documented-rule-diverges-from-enforcement shape — and holding the line would have forced 45 invented source_class values, which is worse than an absent field. Both remain STRONGLY RECOMMENDED and are surfaced by a validator WARN.

completed_tasks.description: Tasks that closed having produced evidence. Two of this list's item types were corrected in v0.131.0 against four months of real records, and `required` was relaxed in v0.130.0 for the same reason: nothing had ever validated against it, because closures were left in `pending_tasks` -- whose item schema constrains neither field. AN UNUSED SCHEMA DRIFTS SILENTLY, and the drift is only visible the moment something finally uses it.

closed_without_evidence.description: Tasks that closed WITHOUT producing evidence — abandoned, cancelled, stalled-out. DELIBERATELY DOES NOT REQUIRE `source_class`: that field classifies where EVIDENCE came from, and a task that produced none has no source class. /log-evidence was corrected on 2026-08-03 for telling authors to write `source_class: cancelled`, a task outcome wearing an evidence field's name that the enum rejects. `closure_reason` carries the meaning instead, and is required here for exactly that reason.

closure_reason.description: Why it closed without evidence. Not optional: an undated, unexplained closure is indistinguishable from a dropped task.
